post_ship_review.summary: Mirrors the 8 fixes applied to the ZH source (diffusion_distillation_tutorial.md, see its sidecar for the full finding-by-finding rationale): the EMA-drop 'loss degenerates to 0' argument corrected to explain the real BYOL/SimSiam-style collapse risk (dropping stop-gradient on the target branch too, not parameter sharing itself); TrigFlow boundary noise corrected from standard N(0,I) to N(0, sigma_d^2 I) for variance-preservation, in both prose and the trigflow_xt()/scm_loss() code; iCT's pseudo-Huber constant given its missing sqrt(D) scaling and the lognormal schedule rebuilt as a deterministic Karras/EDM grid + discretized lognormal index-weighting; ADD's distillation loss un-mischaracterized from a plain teacher-multi-step pixel MSE to score-distillation (re-noise + one-shot teacher denoise) across prose, two comparison tables, the ADDTrainer code, and Q9/Q17/Q23; DMD2's 'GAN-free' cheat-sheet mislabel corrected to point at DMD v1 instead; Reflow's 'optimal transport' / 'straight lines are the OT solution' overreach softened to Theorem 3.6's actual non-increasing-cost guarantee, and 'v(x,t) has no t-dependence' un-conflated from 'constant velocity along one fixed trajectory' (Q8/Q19 included); DINOv2's 518-resolution limit for ADD un-hardened to an interpolatable soft limit, with the discriminator-capacity argument flagged as engineering intuition rather than a paper-verbatim conclusion (Q9/Q23 included); and a light-touch caveat added at rCM/Flow-OPD's first mentions to double-check exact arXiv ids/numbers against the latest revision. The REFUTED finding (FLUX.1-schnell attributed to LADD) was left untouched in both editions — Black Forest Labs' own model card makes the same claim.
